channel.title: Looking Glass
channel.description: Looking Glass — local AI research companion. Update feed.

item.description:
Looking Glass 0.9.0 — talk to Alice, and hear her back

  • Talk instead of typing. Click the mic to enter voice mode, then hold the space bar and speak — let go and it sends. Double-tap the space bar to keep the mic on for a longer thought, and tap the mic again to leave.
  • The mic only listens when you ask it to. Voice mode arms it rather than leaving it open, so a phone call in the same room never ends up in your message.
  • Alice reads her replies aloud in voice mode. She speaks the conversational part and leaves tables, lists and code on screen — you hear an answer rather than a document being recited.
  • The message box becomes a live voice display while you speak, and warms in colour so it is always obvious when the mic is open.
  • She learns the words you use. A place name or term she mishears once, and you correct, is remembered — so she gets it right next time.
  • When she is unsure of a word she hands it back for a quick edit instead of sending it, so a misheard name never goes out silently.
  • Read aloud works on any message, not just in voice mode — hover a reply and press the speaker. Choose a voice and speed in Settings → System → Voice.

Requires macOS 26. Speech recognition runs entirely on your Mac; nothing you say is uploaded.

Looking Glass 0.8.12 — a calmer chat while Alice works

  • The message box locks while Alice is working, with a soft light running around its border — you can always tell a response is still in progress (especially during long tool calls), and only Stop stays active.
  • Big formatted responses no longer flood the chat: Alice's reply stays in its bubble, and the document arrives as a compact card — click to open it in the report viewer.
  • While a document is being written, a live "Composing document…" counter shows progress instead of raw markdown scrolling past.
  • The report viewer has a new rendering engine that handles huge documents smoothly — table-heavy responses that could freeze the app now open fast and scroll silky, in both light and dark.

Looking Glass 0.8.11 — on-device image tools: OCR, editing, and 4× AI upscale

  • Paste text from a screenshot — a picture that's mostly text becomes editable text in the message box, read on-device with Vision (instant, no model call). Pasting, dragging, or attaching images all work now, with an attach button in the input bar.
  • Edit images right in the viewer — resize, crop, and export to PNG/JPEG/HEIF, with a before/after comparison slider.
  • Upscale a generated image 4× on the Neural Engine — a new super-resolution model (RealPLKSR) adds real detail, with a Detail dial to tune it. Downloads a ~30 MB model once.
  • More reliable image generation — the lightweight chat model no longer trips over invalid image-model names.

Looking Glass 0.8.10 — model picker & launch screen fixes

  • The per-chat model button now shows the model's name and variant (e.g. "gemma4:26b"), not just its size — so it's always clear which model a chat is using.
  • Launch screen: Alice now stands out clearly against the dark background.

Looking Glass 0.8.9 — image generation, a real image viewer, and tidier files

  • Generate images right in chat — Alice creates them with your local model and shows them inline, with a full-screen viewer: zoom, pan, copy, and reveal in Finder.
  • Files you create stay organized — generated images, documents, and downloads land in their own folders. Pick your save location in Settings → System → Files.
  • More reliable tool use on the lightweight chat model — it now actually runs tools (image generation, search, files) instead of just describing them.
  • System monitor now lists every running model with its own memory use.
  • Your MCP servers and custom skills now survive app updates.

Looking Glass 0.8.8 — UI polish, a new launch screen, and a refreshed icon

  • New launch screen: full-body Alice greets you with a Wonderland speech bubble — tap it for another quip.
  • Refreshed app icon — a glossier, more refined looking-glass.
  • New Wonderland avatars, roomier chat bubbles, a cleaner glass background, and tidier Settings labels.
  • In-app model registry plus a per-chat model switcher right in the message bar — change the model for one chat without touching your global default.

Looking Glass 0.8.7 — smarter, faster default (gemma4:26b)

  • New default chat model: gemma4:26b — bigger and noticeably faster than the previous default, with the same honest Alice voice. A clear quality + speed upgrade on Apple Silicon.
  • The lighter gemma4:12b remains available as a low-RAM option via Settings → Model.

Looking Glass 0.8.6 — Consult the big model

  • New "Consult the big model" action on Alice's replies: when a local answer isn't deep enough, tap to re-run that question on a larger cloud model — Alice will also suggest it herself on genuinely hard asks. Your conversation only leaves the machine when you tap.
  • Deep Research now runs on a large cloud model for much greater depth, regardless of the model picker.
  • Cloud models are clearly badged in the model picker, and cloud-generated replies are marked — so it's always obvious when an answer left your machine.

Looking Glass 0.8.5 — honesty polish + model tracking

  • Alice is sharper about not faking it: she no longer answers "yes, I know it" when you mention something she hasn't verified, and when she looks something up she now tells you what she found before continuing
  • Each reply now records which model produced it (including mid-conversation model switches) — groundwork for clearer diagnostics and model comparison

Looking Glass 0.8.4 — Alice tells the truth (quality fixes)

  • Alice no longer fabricates confident details about things she doesn't actually know (films, books, people, dates). She now admits when she's unsure, looks it up, and tells you what she found
  • New default chat model: gemma4:12b — doesn't confabulate world-knowledge the way the previous default did, and holds Alice's voice. The faster model is still available per-chat via Settings → Model
  • Fixes an occasional "Ollama HTTP 500" error appearing as a reply after a tool call — the agent now retries transparently

Looking Glass 0.8.3 — hotfix: sidecar startup after Homebrew Python upgrade

  • Fixes "Ollama offline" on launch caused by the embedded Python sidecar failing to start after a Homebrew Python patch upgrade (the bundled interpreter linked to a version-pinned path that gets deleted on upgrade)
  • The embedded interpreter now links to a stable path and is re-signed at build time, so it survives future Homebrew Python patch upgrades

Looking Glass 0.8.2 — Apple Intelligence utilities + faster default model

  • Apple Intelligence utilities: auto-titles new conversations after the first exchange, generates a one-sentence description when you save a message to a project's memory bank, and expands sidebar search queries with synonyms for better recall — all on-device and private
  • Toggle in Settings → System to enable/disable Apple Intelligence features
  • Default chat model updated to qwen3.5:4b-mlx — stronger personality, 64 tok/s on Apple Silicon, half the RAM of the previous default. 9b-mlx still available via Settings → Model

Looking Glass 0.8.0 — Deep Research

  • Deep Research mode: toggle in the input bar — Alice searches multiple sources, synthesizes a full cited report, and saves it as a markdown file
  • Research Report Panel: slide-in panel covers the full window with a blurred backdrop; font size and line height respect your Settings values; tap outside or press Escape to close
  • Live research progress: banner tracks each phase — "Searching the web (N)… → Reading sources (N)… → Saving report… → Report ready"
  • "View Report" button persists across sessions — if the file still exists, the button returns when you reopen the conversation
  • In-chat handoff: after saving, Alice gives a 100–150 word summary with highlights and invites corrections — full report stays in the panel
  • "Write that down": in normal chat, saying anything like "write that down" or "save this" triggers an immediate file_write from the conversation — no confirmation needed

Looking Glass 0.7.5 — Settings & Polish

  • Settings panel restructured into five tabs: Style, System, Skills, MCP, About
  • Skills management: import .md skill files, list and delete skills from the UI
  • MCP Servers management: add/remove servers, live status dots, restart banner
  • User name field: Alice addresses you by name; avatar initials update to match
  • Focus field polish: consistent glass-material border animation across all inputs and search bars
  • System focus rings suppressed app-wide — no more blue halos on buttons at launch
  • Project settings button updated to folder icon

Looking Glass 0.7.2 — Performance fix

  • Fixed app freezing when resizing the window or scrolling through messages with heavy markdown — chat bubbles now skip re-rendering on layout passes when their content hasn't changed

Looking Glass 0.7.1 — Bugfix

  • Fixed: right-clicking a project and choosing "Edit Project…" showed a blank sheet instead of the edit form

Looking Glass 0.7.0 — Tool Calls, System Monitor polish, Project colors

  • Tool Calls panel: global activity log with Current/All filter, search, and expandable result cards — see every tool Alice runs in real time
  • System Monitor polish: Ollama logo tints correctly in dark/light mode; all monitor icons are now white (dark) / black (light) for clarity
  • Project colors: choose from 8 colors when creating a project — folder icons and the project back-button tint to match
  • Edit Project: name, description, and color are now editable (pencil button in the project header or right-click context menu on any project row)
  • Sidebar polish: avatar 2px white/black scheme-aware borders; floating sidebar with clean rounded corners (no bleed); search fields with focus animation

Requires macOS 26, Ollama, and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.6.5 — Liquid Glass UI

  • macOS 26+ native Liquid Glass throughout — circular glass rail buttons, floating sidebar panel, .glassEffect() on bubbles, input bar, and tool cards
  • Wonderland v2 avatars: Caterpillar (Tools), White Rabbit (System), Mad Hatter (Settings) — full kawaii/chibi cast with disc-tint colours
  • Third backdrop "White Rabbit" — Alice and the Rabbit walking, light + dark variants. Settings now has Glass / Wonderland / White Rabbit
  • Edge blur: 80pt top / 120pt bottom gradient mask on the chat scroll view
  • Alice easter egg: large avatar centred in the chat until the first conversation loads
  • Model panel separators now edge-to-edge; sidebar floats with equal window margins and a hairline border

Requires macOS 26, Ollama, and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.6.0 — UI Polish

  • Scroll-edge blur: message bubbles genuinely defocus as they approach the top/bottom edges (real Gaussian blur via .scrollTransition, not just a fade)
  • Sidebar font sizes bumped +2pt across the board — titles are now 24pt heading-weight, chat rows and previews are more readable
  • Model panel: larger model names (16pt) and badge text (14pt)
  • Panel header avatar alignment fixed — no more 2px vertical shift when switching panels
  • Glass edge zones tightened: top 70px / bottom 90px with a dead-zone that keeps blur close to the edge

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.5.0

  • MCP server support: any MCP server declared in config.toml is spawned at startup and its tools are immediately available to Alice — no code changes needed. Ships with MemoryCentral connected (9 cross-project memory tools)
  • Alice can now search, recall, and save memories across all your projects using semantic and keyword search

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.4.0

  • Skills: Alice now has step-by-step playbooks (skills) for multi-step tasks. Ships with a deep-research skill — she searches multiple angles, reads the sources, and saves a cited report. Add your own by dropping a SKILL.md in sidecar/skills/
  • Auto model routing: Alice picks the right model for each request — fast chat model for conversation, coding model for code tasks, deep-research model for in-depth dives. No manual switching needed
  • Image paste → vision: paste or drag an image into the input bar, Alice describes it using a vision model without swapping her main model out

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.3.0

Projects are now a real working surface — Alice understands the folder she's in, and remembers across conversations.

  • Project awareness: in a project, Alice knows its name, description, and folder, and scopes file/shell tools to it
  • Memory: save notes to a project's memory-bank — conversationally ("remember that…") or with a per-message "Save to memory" button — and recall them in later chats
  • Per-project default model and an "Auto" model picker
  • Sidecar lifecycle: clean shutdown on quit, stale-process cleanup on launch, and a keep_alive setting so models free memory on their own
  • Polish: right-aligned message actions, clearer Ollama error messages

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.2.0

  • Persistence & Projects: conversation history (SQLite + full-text search), folder-bound Projects, rename/delete chats
  • Selectable chat font with sans + monospace pairing (Settings → Appearance → Chat Font)
  • GitHub-flavored markdown rendering — headings, blockquotes, tables, task lists
  • New app icon; contrast/elevation polish across bubbles, cards, and the sidebar
  • ⌘, opens Settings

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.

Looking Glass 0.1.0

First release. Native SwiftUI chat with Alice, running locally on Ollama.

  • Streaming chat with a glass UI (rail + collapsible sidebar, light/dark, Wonderland theme)
  • 9 built-in tools: file ops, shell, web search, calculator, pdf extract, and more
  • Multi-turn agent loop with inline tool-call cards
  • Markdown rendering, monospace fonts, adjustable line height
  • Configurable Ollama URL, per-tool toggles, custom avatar, editable system prompt

Requires Ollama and Homebrew Python on the host.
